inputs.goal:
Perform quality control and adapter trimming on the paired-end Tumor and Normal 
samples located in the INPUT_DIR. Run FastQC on the raw reads, trim them using 
Cutadapt with the provided adapters.fa file, and run FastQC again on the trimmed reads. 
Finally, use MultiQC to aggregate all FastQC reports and Cutadapt logs into a 
single summary report. Write all outputs to WORK_DIR.

Perform quality control and adapter trimming on the paired-end Tumor and Normal 
samples located in the INPUT_DIR. Run FastQC on the raw reads, trim them using 
Cutadapt with the provided adapters.fa file, and run FastQC again on the trimmed reads. 
Finally, use MultiQC to aggregate all FastQC reports and Cutadapt logs into a 
single summary report. Write all outputs to WORK_DIR.

work_dir_structure.input: WORK_DIR/input/  — staged input data (read-only, do not write here)
work_dir_structure.steps: WORK_DIR/steps/  — one subdirectory per executed step (NN_rulename/)
work_dir_structure.logs: WORK_DIR/logs/   — per-rule log files written automatically
work_dir_structure.snakefile: WORK_DIR/Snakefile — accumulating workflow, appended each step

path_conventions.input_files: Relative to WORK_DIR/input/. Example: 'samples/A.fastq' resolves to WORK_DIR/input/samples/A.fastq
path_conventions.output_files: Relative to this step's directory. Example: 'A.bam' resolves to WORK_DIR/steps/NN_rulename/A.bam
path_conventions.chained_inputs: To use a prior step's output as input, prefix with 'steps/NN_rulename/'. Example: 'steps/01_bwa_mem_A/A.bam'
path_conventions.never_use: Absolute paths, environment variable names, or bare filenames without the correct prefix.

results.name: fastqc
results.description: Generate fastq qc statistics using fastqc.

outputs.name: fastqc
outputs.description: Generate fastq qc statistics using fastqc.
outputs.example_rule:
rule fastqc:
    input:
        "reads/{sample}.fastq",
    output:
        html="qc/fastqc/{sample}.html",
        zip="qc/fastqc/{sample}_fastqc.zip", # the suffix _fastqc.zip is necessary for multiqc to find the file. If not using multiqc, you are free to choose an arbitrary filename
    params:
        extra="--quiet",
        mem_overhead_factor=0.1,
    log:
        "logs/fastqc/{sample}.log",
    threads: 1
    resources:
        mem_mb = 1024,
    wrapper:
        "master/bio/fastqc"

outputs.name: cutadapt-pe
outputs.example_rule:
rule cutadapt:
    input:
        ["reads/{sample}.1.fastq", "reads/{sample}.2.fastq"],
    output:
        fastq1="trimmed/{sample}.1.fastq",
        fastq2="trimmed/{sample}.2.fastq",
        qc="trimmed/{sample}.qc.txt",
    params:
        # https://cutadapt.readthedocs.io/en/stable/guide.html#adapter-types
        adapters="-a AGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCAC -g AGATCGGAAGAGCACACGT -A AGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCAC -G AGATCGGAAGAGCACACGT",
        # https://cutadapt.readthedocs.io/en/stable/guide.html#
        extra="--minimum-length 1 -q 20",
    log:
        "logs/cutadapt/{sample}.log",
    threads: 4  # set desired number of threads here
    wrapper:
        "master/bio/cutadapt/pe"
